dimensions.title: People
dimensions.question: Who lives in Arkansas, where, and under what human conditions?

baseline_evidence.label: Statewide population (ACS 5-year)
baseline_evidence.note: ACS state aggregate — context, not county baseline.

baseline_evidence.label: Designated-county population change 2020 to 2023
baseline_evidence.pattern: Most designated rural counties in the observation set lost population 2020–2023; White and Van Buren gained.

dimensions.problem_diagnosis: Arkansas is not demographically uniform. Designated rural counties in the Living Systems set show simultaneous population loss and elevated poverty — the inherited geography of decline that any prosperity program must confront without inventing statewide averages as local truth.
dimensions.existing_system_mechanics: Population, poverty, and income are currently measured through federal statistical systems (ACS, PEP, SAIPE) and used unevenly in state budget politics. No single Arkansas NOW dashboard previously joined people → households → budget → assets → leakage.
gaps: Full 75-county PEP/SAIPE panel not yet normalized into the public NOW surface (designated-county set bound).
Age structure, disability prevalence, labor-force participation, and urban/rural distribution need statewide primary binds beyond ACS headline.
Migration origin/destination flows not yet bound as FACT series.

dimensions.title: Households
dimensions.question: What pressures define the Arkansas household balance sheet today?

baseline_evidence.label: Household Prosperity framework (Stage 2)
baseline_evidence.note: Framework exists; Pass 3.1 populates NOW reality into income/poverty anchors — full cost stack is Pass 3.2 unabridged.

dimensions.problem_diagnosis: The unit of success is the household, but the inherited fiscal machine is organized around agencies and appropriations. Pass 3.1 establishes that poverty and income variation across counties is large enough that statewide averages alone cannot diagnose household prosperity.
dimensions.existing_system_mechanics: Households experience the state through wages, prices, taxes, transfers (esp. DHS/Medicaid), and local property/school finance — not through agency org charts.
dimensions.cc_implication: Every later unabridged category must show the transmission path to household Prosperity Surplus or necessary public goods — or be flagged.

dimensions.title: Economy
dimensions.question: What is the scale and structure of Arkansas production and labor income today?

derived.label: Private wages as share of 2024 GDP

dimensions.problem_diagnosis: Arkansas has a large production and wage base while the state operating machine still depends primarily on taxing household and retail flows (IIT + sales). The NOW problem is not absence of economy — it is how surplus, ownership, and public revenue are structured relative to household prosperity.
gaps: Industry composition, agriculture/manufacturing detail, import/export, and corporate concentration require deeper primary binds (Pass 3.4 / 3.6).
Ownership patterns statewide remain partially evidenced.

dimensions.problem_diagnosis: The inherited government finance system is a tax-and-appropriate machine organized by agency, not by economic function or household effect. Surpluses and earmarks coexist with structural dependence on IIT/sales and large recurring transfer/custody blocks.

dimensions.title: Productive Assets
dimensions.question: What does Arkansas actually own or possess the capability to produce with?

baseline_evidence.label: Official program catalog scale (prior bind)
baseline_evidence.note: Strategic capacity catalog — inventory presence, not asset valuation.

baseline_evidence.label: Higher education GR Allocation A
baseline_evidence.note: Appropriation is not the same as capital stock.

dimensions.problem_diagnosis: Arkansas possesses real productive capacity, but the NOW corpus does not yet have a full public asset register or capital stock. Pass 3.1 locks the question and binds what is already evidenced without fabricating valuations.
dimensions.cc_implication: Productive Systems (3.6) and Money/Ownership (3.4) must inventory and govern assets; NOW refuses fake precision.

dimensions.title: Money Leakage & Dependency
dimensions.question: Where can we demonstrate money leaving Arkansas — and where must we label uncertainty?
dimensions.honesty_rule: Do not pretend a perfect statewide leakage number exists yet. Construct the evidence.

evidence_channels.note: Insurance premium tax GR line moved sharply; not a leakage identity by itself.

dimensions.problem_diagnosis: Leakage and dependency are structurally central, but over-precise statewide leakage totals would be ILLUSTRATION pretending to be FACT. Pass 3.1 establishes the evidence channels and refuses fake closure.
dimensions.claim_class_guard: Any future single leakage percentage must be labeled MODEL or ILLUSTRATION until multi-channel primary binds clear Stage 4.

current_state_ledger_join.architecture: Revenue source → expenditure/obligation → beneficiary/function → recurring/nonrecurring → federal/state/local dependency → productive/maintenance/consumption classification → replacement sensitivity

definitions.CONSUME: Immediate operating use that does not leave a lasting productive asset; includes many custody and consumption services.
definitions.MAINTAIN: Keeps existing capability, infrastructure, or service capacity from degrading.
definitions.PROTECT: Public safety, rights enforcement, risk containment, and protective regulation.
definitions.TRANSFER: Cash or in-kind transfer to households, providers, or governments without creating a state-owned productive asset.
definitions.INVEST: Spending expected to raise future productive capability of people, firms, or places.
definitions.BUILD_ASSET: Creates or expands durable physical, digital, or institutional assets.
definitions.GENERATE_RETURN: Spending structured to produce recurring public income or retained surplus for public purpose.

expenditure_taxonomy.method: Analytical classification of economic function — not ideological labels. Applied first to FY2026 GR Allocation A selected patterns; full all-funds anthropology remains multi-year ingest work within the NOW corpus.

problem_diagnosis.one_sentence: Arkansas inherited a capable but leaky political-economic operating system: real people and production, agency-organized public finance dependent on taxing household/retail flows, large recurring transfer and custody blocks, incomplete public asset visibility, and no integrated NOW dashboard joining people → households → money → assets → leakage.
structural_problems: Agency budget optics hide economic function (taxonomy gap).
IIT + sales dominance ties public revenue to household cashflow stress.
DHS/corrections scale creates Dependency Rule constraints on naive cuts.
Rural designated counties show decline patterns masked by statewide averages.
Leakage/dependency discussed rhetorically more often than measured honestly.

cc_model_role_of_now.role: NOW is the starting balance sheet and judgment baseline — not the proposal stack.

cc_model_role_of_now.ownership: Inherited ownership/control is incompletely mapped; NOW states the gap rather than inventing a public-ownership conclusion.
cc_model_role_of_now.household_effects: Statewide and designated-county income/poverty bound; full Prosperity Surplus unabridged in 3.2.
cc_model_role_of_now.government_market_roles: Government today = tax/appropriate/regulate/transfer; markets = QCEW-scale private production. CC later reallocates roles — NOW describes inheritance.
cc_model_role_of_now.arkansas_implementation: All unabridged categories must plug into this NOW baseline.

cc_model_role_of_now.dependencies: Federal funds, Medicaid continuity, corrections medical costs, earmarks, local property/school finance.
cc_model_role_of_now.risks: Misreading surplus as reform; using ACS averages as local truth; inventing leakage totals.

counterarguments.claim: A surplus proves the system is healthy.
counterarguments.response: Surplus is a cash timing fact, not a household-prosperity or asset-formation proof. Taxonomy and county divergence can worsen while surplus exists.
Designated-county PEP/SAIPE show material divergence; averages hide the inherited geography of decline.

counterarguments.claim: We should wait for perfect all-funds data before diagnosing.
counterarguments.response: NOW locks diagnosis architecture and bound facts now; incomplete series are labeled — not filled with invention — and queued for ingest.

certification.statement: Pass 3.1 establishes the definitive Arkansas NOW diagnosis architecture and binds primary-source evidence across six X-Ray dimensions, the Budget X-Ray signature asset, expenditure taxonomy, sources, counterarguments, and open validation questions — without inventing leakage totals, all-funds federal shares, or COUNTABLE dollars. Remaining series incompleteness is explicit and assigned, not hidden.
